project.title: Personal task management system
project.scope: A personal task management system for tracking daily tasks and generating status reports. Page 1 manages the user's to-do list: create, view, update, delete, and change task status, with a defined task data model and validation rules. Page 2 is a task reporting page that shows an aggregated, filterable, searchable, sortable table with metrics and an Excel export. Where the PRD leaves choices open, such as where the Excel file is generated and the wording of the no-data message, these remain open questions.

stories.title: Create a new task with required fields
stories.i_want: create a new task with its required fields
stories.so_that: I can record a piece of work in my personal task list
stories.business_description: Users need to add tasks to their personal to-do list. Each new task stores a unique ID, a Title, a Description, a Status, a Priority, a Creation Date, a Due Date, a Last Updated Date and a Completion Date. The task is saved in the persistence database, in a new tasks table.
stories.business_value: Without task creation, no other to-do capability (viewing, editing, status changes, reporting) has data to work on. Mandatory titles and date validation keep stored tasks complete and consistent.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user opens the task creation form
acceptance_criteria.when: The user submits the form with a non-empty title and all other required inputs valid
acceptance_criteria.then: The backend stores exactly one new task with a unique ID, and the form shows a success message

acceptance_criteria.given: A user opens the task creation form
acceptance_criteria.when: The user submits the form with an empty title
acceptance_criteria.then: The backend rejects the task, no task is stored, and the form shows an error message that names the title field as mandatory

acceptance_criteria.given: A user opens the task creation form with a Creation Date of 2024-05-10
acceptance_criteria.when: The user submits a Due Date of 2024-05-09
acceptance_criteria.then: The backend rejects the task with an error stating that the Due Date cannot be earlier than the Creation Date, and no task is stored

acceptance_criteria.given: A user opens the task creation form with a Creation Date of 2024-05-10
acceptance_criteria.when: The user submits a Due Date of 2024-05-10
acceptance_criteria.then: The backend accepts the task because the Due Date is not earlier than the Creation Date

acceptance_criteria.given: A new task has been stored
acceptance_criteria.when: The task is read from the database
acceptance_criteria.then: The task has the fields ID, Title, Description, Status, Priority, Creation Date, Due Date, Last Updated Date and Completion Date, and Completion Date is empty

acceptance_criteria.given: The backend create request fails because of a database error
acceptance_criteria.when: The user submits the task creation form
acceptance_criteria.then: The form shows an error message and does not show the task as created

acceptance_criteria.given: A create request has been sent but the backend has not yet responded
acceptance_criteria.when: The form is waiting for the response
acceptance_criteria.then: The frontend does not show a success message or add the task to any list

edge_cases: The PRD does not state the exact wording of the success message; the wording is an open question.
The PRD does not state whether Due Date is mandatory; if it is left empty, the behaviour is an open question.
The PRD does not say whether a title containing only spaces counts as empty; this is an open question.
The PRD does not state the default values of Status and Priority on creation; this is an open question.
A Due Date equal to the Creation Date is valid.
Completion Date stays empty on creation because the task is not completed yet.
definition_of_done: The tasks table migration creates every task data-model field, including the unique ID and Completion Date.
POST /tasks rejects an empty title and a Due Date earlier than the Creation Date, with clear error responses.
The form shows a success message only after the backend confirms the save, and an error message on failure.
The form does not add the task to any list before the backend responds.
Automated tests cover the valid, empty-title and date-order cases.

stories.title: View the task list with status and priority indicators
stories.as_a: user with a personal to-do list
stories.i_want: to view my task list with a status and a priority indicator on each task
stories.so_that: I can see the state and urgency of my tasks at a glance on the to-do management page
stories.business_description: The to-do management page lets the user manage their personal task list. This story delivers the read-only task list view: it shows the user's tasks, each with a status indicator and a priority indicator, and shows loading, empty and error states. The list refreshes automatically when a task is changed. Creating, editing, deleting and changing status are handled by other stories.
stories.business_value: The user can see all their tasks and their state in one place, so they know what is open, in progress or completed and how urgent each task is.

acceptance_criteria.given: The user has at least one task in their personal task list
acceptance_criteria.when: The user opens the to-do management page
acceptance_criteria.then: The task list view shows each of the user's tasks, with a status indicator and a priority indicator on every row

acceptance_criteria.given: A task has status Open, In Progress or Completed
acceptance_criteria.when: The task list view renders that task
acceptance_criteria.then: The status indicator shows the task's current status text and a visually distinct mark for each of the three values

acceptance_criteria.given: A task has priority Low, Medium or High
acceptance_criteria.when: The task list view renders that task
acceptance_criteria.then: The priority indicator shows the task's priority text and a visually distinct mark for each of the three values

acceptance_criteria.given: The task list request to the backend has not yet completed
acceptance_criteria.when: The task list view is displayed
acceptance_criteria.then: A loading state is shown and no task rows or empty-state text are shown

acceptance_criteria.given: The user has no tasks
acceptance_criteria.when: The backend returns an empty task list
acceptance_criteria.then: The empty state is shown and no task rows are shown

acceptance_criteria.given: The task list request to the backend fails with an error
acceptance_criteria.when: The task list view is displayed
acceptance_criteria.then: The error state is shown with a message, and the loading state is no longer shown

acceptance_criteria.given: The task list is displayed and the user creates, updates, deletes or changes the status of a task
acceptance_criteria.when: The backend confirms the change succeeded
acceptance_criteria.then: The task list is reloaded from the backend and shows the changed task without a manual page refresh

acceptance_criteria.given: The backend read endpoint for all tasks is called
acceptance_criteria.when: The request is received
acceptance_criteria.then: The backend returns only the tasks belonging to the requesting user

edge_cases: A task whose status or priority value is outside the allowed values cannot be produced by the data model, so the indicators need only handle Open, In Progress, Completed, Low, Medium and High (open question: the PRD does not state how the view should display a value outside these sets)
The list refresh happens only after the backend confirms a change; the view must not show the changed state before that confirmation

A read by ID request for a task that does not exist returns a task-not-found error, which this story exposes through the backend read endpoint but does not display in a dedicated screen (open question: the PRD does not say where a single-task view is shown)
The PRD does not state how many tasks the list shows per page or whether it paginates (open question)
The PRD does not state how the user is authenticated or how tasks are scoped to a user (open question)
definition_of_done: Backend exposes a GET endpoint that returns all tasks for the requesting user, with each task's status and priority
Backend exposes a GET endpoint that returns one task by ID, returning a task-not-found error when the ID does not exist
Backend returns the error responses defined by the shared error handling approach for not-found and internal server or database errors
Task list view renders loading, empty and error states as separate, distinguishable views
Status indicator and priority indicator render for every task row with all allowed values
Task list refetches from the backend after a create, update, delete or status change succeeds, and does not update the list optimistically
Automated tests cover the loading, empty, error and populated states of the task list view
Automated tests cover the GET all and GET by ID endpoints, including the not-found case
Open questions on pagination, authentication scope and single-task display are recorded in the story notes

stories.title: Edit an existing task
stories.i_want: to edit an existing task and save my changes
stories.so_that: my task list reflects the current state of my work
stories.business_description: The user can change the details of a task that already exists. The same form used to create a task is reused in edit mode. The backend validates the changed values and returns a success or error result, and the frontend shows that result only after the backend confirms the change.
stories.business_value: Users can correct and maintain their tasks without deleting and recreating them, which keeps the task list accurate.

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing task with a valid title and a Due Date not earlier than its Creation Date
acceptance_criteria.when: the user opens the edit form, changes the title, and submits the form
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend stores the new title and the task shows the new title in the list after the backend returns success

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing task being edited in the form
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clears the title field and submits the form
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend rejects the update, the task keeps its previous title, and an error message stating that the title is mandatory is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing task with Creation Date 2024-05-10
acceptance_criteria.when: the user sets the Due Date to 2024-05-09 and submits the update
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend rejects the update with a validation error, the stored Due Date is unchanged, and an error message is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: a task update request where the backend returns an error
acceptance_criteria.when: the frontend receives the error response
acceptance_criteria.then: the frontend does not show the task as updated and displays an error message

acceptance_criteria.given: a task update request where the backend returns success
acceptance_criteria.when: the frontend receives the success response
acceptance_criteria.then: the frontend displays a success message after the update action

acceptance_criteria.given: a task ID that does not exist in the database
acceptance_criteria.when: an update request is sent for that ID
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend returns a Task Not Found error and no data is changed

edge_cases: Update request for a task that was deleted by another session: the backend returns Task Not Found and the frontend shows an error message.
Title containing only spaces: the PRD does not say whether whitespace-only titles are empty; this is an open question.
Due Date equal to Creation Date: the PRD rejects only dates earlier than the Creation Date, so equal dates are accepted.
Update that fails with an internal server or database error: the frontend shows an error and does not show the task as updated.
Open question: the PRD does not state which fields are editable; whether Creation Date, Status and Completion Date can be changed through the update is not specified.
Open question: the PRD lists a Last Updated Date field but does not state that it must change on each update; this needs confirmation.
definition_of_done: Update endpoint accepts changes to a task by ID and returns the updated task on success.
Backend rejects an empty title and a Due Date earlier than the Creation Date with a validation error, and stores nothing in those cases.
Backend returns Task Not Found for an unknown ID and an error for invalid input, as defined by the shared error handling.
Frontend reuses the create/edit form in edit mode with the existing values pre-filled.
Frontend shows a success or error message after every update action.
Frontend does not show a task as updated until the backend returns success.
Open questions about editable fields and Last Updated Date are recorded and answered before release.

stories.title: Delete a task after confirmation
stories.i_want: to delete a task after confirming the deletion
stories.so_that: tasks I no longer need are removed from my list
stories.business_description: The user can delete a task from their list. Deletion requires a confirmation prompt. The frontend shows a success or error message after the delete action, and shows a success state only after the backend confirms the deletion.
stories.business_value: Users can remove tasks they no longer need, and accidental deletions are reduced by the confirmation prompt.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with a known ID exists in the user's list
acceptance_criteria.when: the user selects delete on that task and cancels the confirmation prompt
acceptance_criteria.then: no delete request is sent to the backend and the task remains in the list

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with a known ID exists in the user's list
acceptance_criteria.when: the user selects delete and confirms the prompt
acceptance_criteria.then: the frontend sends a delete request for that task ID, the backend responds with success, and the frontend shows a success message and removes the task from the list

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with a known ID exists in the user's list
acceptance_criteria.when: the user confirms the delete prompt and the backend returns an error
acceptance_criteria.then: the task remains visible in the list and the frontend shows an error message; no success state is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: a task ID that does not exist in storage
acceptance_criteria.when: a delete request is sent for that ID
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend responds with a task-not-found error and no data is changed

acceptance_criteria.given: the database is unavailable during a delete request
acceptance_criteria.when: the backend attempts to delete the task
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend responds with an internal server or database error and the task is not reported as deleted

edge_cases: A delete request for a task ID that does not exist returns a task-not-found error and changes no data.
The database is unavailable during a delete request: the backend returns an internal server or database error and the task is not reported as deleted.
The backend returns an error after the user confirms: the task stays in the list and no success state is shown.
The PRD does not state whether deletion is permanent or soft. This is an open question for the team.
The PRD does not state how the frontend should behave if the delete request times out without a response. This is an open question for the team.
definition_of_done: DELETE /tasks/{id} removes the task with the given ID and returns success.
A delete request for an unknown ID returns a task-not-found error and changes no data.
A database or internal error during delete returns an error response and the task is not reported as deleted.
The delete action opens a confirmation prompt; cancelling sends no request.
Confirming sends the delete request; the success message is shown and the task is removed only after success.
An error response shows an error message and keeps the task visible.
No success state is shown before the backend confirms the deletion.
Automated tests cover the confirm, cancel, success, not-found and server-error paths.

stories.title: Mark a task as Completed or revert it to Open
stories.i_want: mark a task as Completed or revert a Completed task back to Open
stories.so_that: I can track which tasks are done on my to-do list
stories.business_description: Users need to record progress on their tasks. A task moves between Open and Completed. The backend stores each change, and the task list reflects only changes the backend has confirmed.
stories.business_value: Users can see which work is finished and which is still open, and the stored status stays accurate.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with status Open exists
acceptance_criteria.when: the user marks the task as Completed
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend stores the status Completed and the task list shows the task with status Completed

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with status Completed exists
acceptance_criteria.when: the user reverts the task to Open
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend stores the status Open and the task list shows the task with status Open

acceptance_criteria.given: the status change request for an existing task fails in the backend
acceptance_criteria.when: the frontend receives the failure
acceptance_criteria.then: the task list still shows the previous status and an error message is displayed

acceptance_criteria.given: a status change request is pending and the backend has not responded yet
acceptance_criteria.when: the task list is displayed
acceptance_criteria.then: the row still shows the previous status and no success message is displayed

acceptance_criteria.given: a status change request is sent for a task ID that does not exist
acceptance_criteria.when: the backend processes the request
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend returns a task not found error and no stored task changes

acceptance_criteria.given: a status change request is sent with a status value other than Open or Completed
acceptance_criteria.when: the backend validates the request
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend rejects the request with an invalid input error and the stored status does not change

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is marked as Completed
acceptance_criteria.when: the backend saves the change
acceptance_criteria.then: the Completion Date field of the task is populated with the time of the change

edge_cases: A task is marked Completed while it is already Completed, or reverted to Open while it is already Open: the PRD does not say whether this is rejected or accepted as a no-op; this is an open question.
A task is reverted to Open: the PRD does not state whether the Completion Date is cleared or kept; this is an open question.
The status change request fails with an internal server or database error: the stored status stays unchanged and the frontend shows an error message.
The status change request is still pending when the user views the task list: the row keeps the previous status until the backend confirms the change.
definition_of_done: A status change endpoint accepts only Open and Completed and stores the new status.
Marking a task Completed populates its Completion Date with the time of the change.
Task not found and invalid status responses are returned as specified by the error handling rules.
The frontend shows the new status only after the backend confirms the change and never before.
A pending status change leaves the row at its previous status.
A failed status change leaves the previous status displayed and shows an error message.
The QA test suite passes for all acceptance criteria.

stories.title: View all tasks in a report table with metrics
stories.i_want: see all of my tasks in a table on the Task Reporting page, with Total Tasks, Open Tasks and Completed Tasks metrics
stories.so_that: I can review the status of my whole task list at a glance
stories.business_description: The Task Reporting page gives the user an aggregated view of their own tasks. It shows every task in a table and three metrics computed from those tasks: Total Tasks, Open Tasks and Completed Tasks.
stories.business_value: The user can see how much work is open and how much is completed without opening each task.

acceptance_criteria.given: The user has 5 tasks, 2 with status Open and 3 with status Completed
acceptance_criteria.when: The user opens the Task Reporting page
acceptance_criteria.then: The table shows 5 rows, one per task, and the metrics show Total Tasks 5, Open Tasks 2 and Completed Tasks 3

acceptance_criteria.given: The user has no tasks
acceptance_criteria.when: The user opens the Task Reporting page
acceptance_criteria.then: The table shows no task rows and the metrics show Total Tasks 0, Open Tasks 0 and Completed Tasks 0

acceptance_criteria.given: The report endpoint returns tasks with their Status, Priority and Due Date values
acceptance_criteria.when: The Task Reporting page loads
acceptance_criteria.then: Each table row shows the task Title, Status, Priority and Due Date from the endpoint response, with no values added or changed by the page

acceptance_criteria.given: A user changes the status of a task from Open to Completed
acceptance_criteria.when: The user reloads the Task Reporting page
acceptance_criteria.then: The Open Tasks metric decreases by 1 and the Completed Tasks metric increases by 1, while Total Tasks stays the same

acceptance_criteria.given: The report endpoint is called without any filter, search or sort parameters
acceptance_criteria.when: The request is processed
acceptance_criteria.then: The response contains all of the user's tasks and the three metric values Total, Open and Completed computed from those tasks

edge_cases: The user has no tasks: the table is empty and all three metrics show 0.
Metric values are computed from the same set of tasks as the table rows, so they always agree with the rows shown.
The PRD does not state the table column order or the date display format; this is an open question for the team.
definition_of_done: The report endpoint returns all of the user's tasks with Title, Status, Priority and Due Date.
The report endpoint returns Total, Open and Completed counts for the user's tasks in the same response.
The Task Reporting page renders one table row per task returned by the endpoint.
The Task Reporting page shows Total Tasks, Open Tasks and Completed Tasks from the endpoint response.
The page shows no task values that differ from the endpoint response.
Automated tests for the table and metrics pass.

stories.title: Filter report tasks by status, priority and date range
stories.as_a: user who reviews my tasks on the task reporting page
stories.i_want: to filter the report tasks by Status, Priority and Date Range
stories.so_that: I can see only the tasks that match the part of my workload I am reviewing
stories.business_description: The reporting page offers Status, Priority and Date Range filters. The backend report API must support filtering so that the page can show only the matching tasks. Searching, sorting and metric aggregation are covered by other stories.
stories.business_value: Users can narrow a long task list to the subset they need to review, without scanning every task on the page.

acceptance_criteria.given: The report contains tasks with Open, In Progress and Completed status
acceptance_criteria.when: The user selects the status filter value Open on the reporting page
acceptance_criteria.then: The report table lists only tasks whose status is Open and no other tasks

acceptance_criteria.given: The report contains tasks with Low, Medium and High priority
acceptance_criteria.when: The user selects the priority filter value High on the reporting page
acceptance_criteria.then: The report table lists only tasks whose priority is High and no other tasks

acceptance_criteria.given: The report contains tasks with dates both inside and outside a chosen range
acceptance_criteria.when: The user sets a Date Range on the reporting page
acceptance_criteria.then: The report table lists only tasks whose date value falls inside the range; the date field used is the open question listed in the edge cases

acceptance_criteria.given: The report API is called with a status, a priority or a date range filter
acceptance_criteria.when: The request is sent with one or more filter values
acceptance_criteria.then: The response contains only the tasks that match the filter values sent, and the count in the response equals the number of returned tasks

edge_cases: The PRD does not state which date field the Date Range filter applies to (Creation Date, Due Date, Completion Date or Last Updated Date). This is an open question and must be decided before the date filter is built.
The PRD does not state whether the range bounds are inclusive. This is an open question.
The PRD does not state whether several filters combine with AND or OR. This is an open question; the API and the page must follow the same rule.
A Date Range where the start date is later than the end date is not defined by the PRD. This is an open question: the API or the page must reject it, and the wording of the message is not specified.
When no task matches the selected filters, the report table has no rows. The PRD does not specify the message or empty state for this case on the report page.

A filter value outside the allowed values (Open, In Progress, Completed for status; Low, Medium, High for priority) is invalid input and must be rejected with the error handling defined in the create task story.
Clearing a filter returns the report to the unfiltered list for that filter.
definition_of_done: The report API accepts status, priority and date range filter parameters and returns only matching tasks.
The API rejects invalid filter values with the standard invalid input error.
The reporting page shows Status, Priority and Date Range filter controls that call the API and update the table.
The date field and combination rule for the Date Range filter are documented and implemented as decided.
Automated tests cover each filter alone, combined filters, an empty result and an invalid filter value.
No optimistic UI is used: the table updates only after the API returns the filtered result.

stories.title: Search report tasks by title
stories.i_want: search my tasks by title on the reporting page
stories.so_that: I can find a specific task in my report without scanning the full table
stories.business_description: The Task Reporting page lets the user type text to search tasks by their title. The backend report API accepts a title search value and returns only the matching tasks.
stories.business_value: Users can locate a single task quickly in a larger report by matching its title, as required by the 'Search: By Title' reporting requirement.

acceptance_criteria.given: the reporting page shows tasks and a title search input is visible
acceptance_criteria.when: the user enters a search text that exactly matches the title of one task and submits the search
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend report API is called with that search text and the table shows only the task(s) whose title contains it

acceptance_criteria.given: the reporting page shows tasks
acceptance_criteria.when: the user enters a search text that matches no task title
acceptance_criteria.then: the table shows no rows and a message stating that no tasks match the search is displayed

acceptance_criteria.given: a search text is entered on the reporting page
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clears the search input
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend report API is called without a title search value and the table shows all tasks again

acceptance_criteria.given: the report API is running and the database holds tasks with titles
acceptance_criteria.when: a client calls the report API with a title search parameter
acceptance_criteria.then: the response contains only tasks whose Title matches the parameter and the response status is 200

edge_cases: Open question: whether the match is exact or partial (contains) is not stated in the PRD; this story assumes a partial match only if the team confirms it.
Open question: whether the match is case-sensitive is not stated in the PRD.
An empty search text is treated as no search; the PRD does not state this explicitly.
Search text containing only spaces: the PRD does not state whether it is trimmed or rejected.
Search combined with status, priority, date range, sorting or export filters: combined behaviour is owned by those stories and must be consistent with this search.
Search text containing special characters must be treated as plain text and must not change the query result (no injection).
definition_of_done: Report API accepts an optional title search parameter and returns only tasks whose Title matches it.
Reporting page has a title search input that calls the API and shows the filtered table.
Empty result state for a search with no matches is shown on the page.
Automated tests cover exact match, partial match behaviour as decided, no match, and cleared search.
Open questions on exact versus partial match and case sensitivity are answered and recorded in the story notes.
Code reviewed and merged into the main branch.

stories.title: Sort report tasks by creation date, due date, status or priority
stories.i_want: to sort the report tasks by Creation Date, Due Date, Status or Priority
stories.so_that: I can review my tasks in the order I need
stories.business_description: The Task Reporting page lets the user sort the task table by Creation Date, Due Date, Status or Priority. The report API accepts a sort field and returns tasks ordered by it.
stories.business_value: Users can find the most urgent or oldest tasks quickly and review the report in a consistent order.

acceptance_criteria.given: The Task Reporting page displays at least two tasks with different Creation Dates
acceptance_criteria.when: The user selects the sort option Creation Date
acceptance_criteria.then: The table rows are reordered so that the Creation Date values are in a single consistent order (ascending or descending, as defined by the sort control) and the sort option shown as selected is Creation Date

acceptance_criteria.given: The Task Reporting page displays tasks with different Due Dates
acceptance_criteria.when: The user selects the sort option Due Date
acceptance_criteria.then: The table rows are reordered by the Due Date field and the sort option shown as selected is Due Date

acceptance_criteria.given: The Task Reporting page displays tasks with different Status values
acceptance_criteria.when: The user selects the sort option Status
acceptance_criteria.then: The table rows are reordered by the Status field and the sort option shown as selected is Status

acceptance_criteria.given: The Task Reporting page displays tasks with different Priority values
acceptance_criteria.when: The user selects the sort option Priority
acceptance_criteria.then: The table rows are reordered by the Priority field and the sort option shown as selected is Priority

acceptance_criteria.given: The report API is called with a sort field of creation_date, due_date, status or priority
acceptance_criteria.when: The request is processed by the backend
acceptance_criteria.then: The response contains the matching tasks ordered by that field

acceptance_criteria.given: The report API is called with a sort field that is not one of creation_date, due_date, status or priority
acceptance_criteria.when: The request is processed by the backend
acceptance_criteria.then: The backend returns an invalid input error and no task data is returned

edge_cases: The PRD does not state the sort direction (ascending or descending) for each option or the default sort order; this is an open question for the sort control.
The PRD does not define the order of Status values (Open, In Progress, Completed) or Priority values (Low, Medium, High) when sorting; this is an open question.
The PRD does not define the order of tasks that share the same sort value; this is an open question.
A sort field outside the four allowed values is rejected with an invalid input error.
definition_of_done: The report API accepts a sort parameter with the values creation_date, due_date, status and priority.
The report API rejects any other sort value with an invalid input error and returns no task data.
The report table offers exactly four sort options: Creation Date, Due Date, Status and Priority.
The selected sort option is shown in the UI and matches the sort applied to the table.
Sort direction and the order of Status and Priority values are documented or confirmed with the product owner.

stories.title: Export the filtered report tasks to an Excel file
stories.i_want: to download the tasks currently shown in the report as an Excel file
stories.so_that: I can use the filtered and sorted task data outside the application
stories.business_description: The Task Reporting page lets the user download task data to an Excel file. The exported file must match the filters and sorting currently applied to the task view. It must have clear column headers, one consistent date format, and a filename that includes the time the file was generated. If there is no data to export, the user sees a message and no file is produced.
stories.business_value: Users can share and analyse the exact task view they are working with, without re-entering filters or manually copying data from the report table.

acceptance_criteria.given: The Task Reporting page is open and at least one task is shown in the report table
acceptance_criteria.when: The user clicks the Export to Excel control
acceptance_criteria.then: An Excel file is downloaded containing the tasks shown in the report

acceptance_criteria.given: The report has Status = Open, Priority = High and a sort by Due Date ascending applied
acceptance_criteria.when: The user exports the report to Excel
acceptance_criteria.then: The file contains only tasks with Status Open and Priority High, in Due Date ascending order, and no other tasks

acceptance_criteria.given: The report is filtered so that no tasks match
acceptance_criteria.when: The user clicks the Export to Excel control
acceptance_criteria.then: No file is downloaded and the message 'No tasks to export' is shown on the page (exact wording is an open question)

acceptance_criteria.given: An Excel file is exported
acceptance_criteria.when: The file is opened
acceptance_criteria.then: The first row contains a column header for every exported field and every date cell uses the same date format

acceptance_criteria.given: A file is exported at a given time
acceptance_criteria.when: The browser saves the file
acceptance_criteria.then: The filename contains the timestamp of the moment the export was generated

acceptance_criteria.given: The team has completed the decision spike on where the Excel file is generated
acceptance_criteria.when: The export is implemented
acceptance_criteria.then: The generation location matches the documented decision and the decision record is linked from the story

edge_cases: The filtered result is empty: no file is produced and the no-data message is shown.
The report contains a single task: the file still has the header row and one data row.
Sorting is applied with equal values in the sort column: the exported order of tied rows is not specified in the PRD (open question).
Tasks with no Completion Date: the value shown in the exported cell is not specified in the PRD (open question).
The exact wording of the no-data message is not specified (open question).
The timestamp format in the filename and the time zone used for it are not specified (open question).
The list of exported columns is not specified beyond 'task data' (open question; assumed to match the columns of the report table).
Very large result sets: maximum export size and any limit are not specified (open question).
definition_of_done: Export control is visible on the Task Reporting page and downloads a file when clicked.
Exported rows match the filters and sort applied to the report at the time of export, verified by automated tests.
Column headers are present in the first row and are human-readable.
All date cells in the file use one date format.
Filename contains a generation timestamp and is unique for each export.
No file is produced when the filtered result is empty, and the no-data message is shown.
The decision on frontend or backend generation is documented with rationale and trade-offs.
Error responses from the export endpoint are handled and shown to the user.

requirements.source_quote: A personal task management system that allows users to track daily tasks and generate status reports.
requirements.statement: The system is a personal task management system for tracking daily tasks and generating status reports.
requirements.context_reason: Introductory product description that states no testable requirement on its own.

requirements.source_quote: The system consists of two main pages.
requirements.statement: The system is composed of two main pages.
requirements.context_reason: Descriptive statement that names the page count but does not specify what the pages are or how they behave; the pages themselves are defined elsewhere in the PRD.

requirements.source_quote: This page allows the user to manage their personal task list.
requirements.statement: The to-do management page lets the user manage their personal task list.
The user can create a new task.
The user can view the task list.
The user can update an existing task.
The user can delete a task.
The user can mark a task as 'Completed'.
The user can revert a 'Completed' task back to 'Open'.
Each task must contain the listed fields.
requirements.context_reason: Introductory sentence that lists the fields; the listed items are the requirements.

requirements.statement: Each task has a unique ID field.
Each task has a Title field.
Each task has a Description field.
Each task has a Status field whose allowed values are Open, In Progress and Completed.
Each task has a Priority field whose allowed values are Low, Medium and High.
Each task has a Creation Date field.
Each task has a Due Date field.
Each task has a Last Updated Date field.
Each task has a Completion Date field, populated when the task is completed.

requirements.source_quote: Task titles are mandatory; cannot be empty.
requirements.statement: The system rejects a task whose title is empty, so task titles are mandatory.

requirements.source_quote: Due Date cannot be earlier than the Creation Date.
requirements.statement: The system rejects a task whose Due Date is earlier than its Creation Date.

requirements.source_quote: Deleting a task requires a prompt confirmation.
requirements.statement: Deleting a task requires the user to confirm the deletion through a prompt before it is performed.

requirements.source_quote: Success or error messages must be displayed after create/update/delete actions.
requirements.statement: A success or error message is displayed after each create, update and delete task action.

requirements.source_quote: Optimistic UI updates are not allowed: if a Backend action fails, the Frontend must not reflect a successful state.
requirements.statement: The frontend does not show a successful state for a task action unless the backend action has succeeded; optimistic UI updates are not allowed.
The system provides a task list view that displays the user's to-do tasks.
The system provides a form for creating and editing tasks.
The system displays a status indicator and a priority indicator for each task.
The task list view shows a distinct loading state, empty state, and error state.
The task list refreshes automatically when a task is changed.

requirements.source_quote: The Todos should be saved in persistence DB – assume the DB already exits but there will be a need for a new table
requirements.statement: To-do items must be saved in the persistence database, which is assumed to already exist, in a new table created for them.

requirements.source_quote: Endpoints for Create, Read (All & By ID), Update, Delete, and Status Change.
requirements.statement: The backend must expose endpoints to create, read all, read by ID, update, delete, and change the status of to-do items.

requirements.source_quote: Error handling for: Task Not Found, Invalid Input, Missing Mandatory Fields, Deleting/Updating Non-Existent Tasks, and Internal Server/Database Errors. For error handling - Keep it simple
requirements.statement: The backend must handle errors for task not found, invalid input, missing mandatory fields, deleting or updating non-existent tasks, and internal server or database errors, using a simple error handling approach.

requirements.source_quote: This page presents an aggregated view of the user's tasks.
requirements.statement: The Task Reporting page presents an aggregated view of the user's tasks.
The reporting page displays all tasks in a table.
The reporting page lets the user filter tasks by Status, Priority, and Date Range.
The reporting page lets the user search tasks by title.

requirements.source_quote: Sort: By Creation Date, Due Date, Status, or Priority.
requirements.statement: The reporting page lets the user sort tasks by Creation Date, Due Date, Status, or Priority.

requirements.source_quote: Metrics: Total Tasks, Open Tasks, Completed Tasks.
requirements.statement: The reporting page shows the metrics Total Tasks, Open Tasks, and Completed Tasks.
The reporting page lets the user download task data to an Excel file.

requirements.source_quote: The file must reflect the currently applied filters and sorting.
requirements.statement: The exported Excel file must reflect the filters and sorting currently applied to the task view.

requirements.source_quote: Clear column headers and consistent date formatting.
requirements.statement: The exported Excel file must have clear column headers and use one consistent date format throughout.

requirements.source_quote: Filename must include the generation timestamp.
requirements.statement: The filename of the exported Excel file must include the timestamp of when the file was generated.

requirements.source_quote: User-friendly message if there is no data to export.
requirements.statement: When there is no data to export, the system must show a message to the user instead of producing an empty file. The exact wording of the message is not specified and is an open question.

requirements.source_quote: APIs to support filtering, searching, sorting, and metric aggregation.
requirements.statement: The system exposes APIs that support filtering, searching, sorting, and metric aggregation for task reporting.

requirements.source_quote: The architectural decision of whether to generate the Excel file on the Frontend or Backend is left to the development team.
requirements.statement: The development team decides whether the Excel file is generated on the frontend or the backend.
